items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: Well, you only had John Alfred, the drummer.

ctx.x: Well, I got Alan Vann the job with him after Leroy Moore quit. See, I had a broad amount of, well, I don't know how you put it. Troy had depended on me to do things for him, and I would seek the musician, so I told him about Alan Vann's playing, and Troy was always a fella that you had to prove to him, or he never showed that he never was too interested in what you were talking about. So I had Alan to come and rehearse with the band at 520 South Hagbury, and he took him into the band from there. But I don't…
Well, somebody in that band I was going to ask you about. Well, you only had John Alfred, the drummer. Oh, the guitar player.

Oh, John Henry Braggs. He's still living. He's in San Antonio. He doesn't play anymore. Did he sing the blues ever? No. Just played the banjo. He played an old-style banjo, what they call the plectrum banjo, five strings. Mm-hmm. Good musician. His wife was a blues singer, Ed L. Braggs.
